$comment: Tier-2 differential for the wardrobe TRANSFERS service (v4
app/api/v1/wardrobe/transfers/route.ts POST), ported to
quilltap-core::services::wardrobe_transfers::transfer_wardrobe_item.
One committed file drives BOTH sides:
- the v4 oracle (harness/oracle/cases/wardrobe-transfers.test.ts, a JEST
oracle) resets to a fresh copy of the baked fixture per scenario, mocks
getServerSession -> { user: { id: userId } }, forces startup/pepper ready,
doMocks the REAL DB stack (past jest.setup's global mocks) + the real
better-sqlite3-multiple-ciphers cipher binding, then calls the REAL POST
handler and dumps the mount-index tables after each scenario.
- the Rust port (quilltap-harness wardrobe_transfers test) copies the two
fixture DBs per scenario, opens a MAIN + MOUNT Writer, and calls
transfer_wardrobe_item with FROZEN_NOW.
FIXTURE (build-wardrobe-transfers-fixture.ts, two DBs): a users row; a
character owned by that user (REAL repos.characters.create, pinned) with one
wardrobe SOURCE item seeded into its vault (REAL repos.wardrobe.create,
pinned); a slim project row + slim group row (REAL repos.projects/groups.create
-- store-backed, so each already carries a provisioned official store; the
transfer's ensure_official_store FINDS it and just ensures Wardrobe/); a
provisioned Quilltap General store + instance_settings.generalMountPointId with
one archetype item seeded into General/Wardrobe/. All ids/timestamps pinned.
SCENARIOS (each = one POST + one full mount-index dump; fresh fixture copy per
scenario so they are independent):
1. copy character -> general (new uuid + now timestamps; source item stays)
2. move character -> project (provisions/ensures project Wardrobe/; source
item gone; id/timestamps carry over)
3. copy general -> character (new uuid + now; general archetype stays)
4. error: same source == destination (copy character -> character self) ->
badRequest 'Source and destination are the same'
5. error: id collision -- move character -> character (destination already
holds an item with the moved id) -> badRequest 'An item with that ID
already exists at the destination'
NORMALIZATION (harness, shared cross-table/cross-db id-map remap form): minted
ids -> first-appearance tokens across all dumped tables; timestamps -> <ts>;
link chunkCount -> <cc>; doc_mount_chunks EXCLUDED (a v4-only reindex artifact
the Rust storage primitive does not rebuild). FROZEN_NOW is arbitrary; copy
timestamps are minted, so the remap placeholders them either way.
SAFETY: testPepperBase64 is a THROWAWAY 32-byte key (the same one folders/tags/
characters/wardrobe use). NOT the real Friday pepper; safe to commit.
P4.D71 (v4 8600c83f) added the GROUP tier as a SOURCE scope, scanned between
project and General. The fixture therefore also carries a group MEMBERSHIP
for the source character and one item seeded into the group official store's
Wardrobe/ folder, plus three scenarios: move the group item OUT to the
character (the round trip that was impossible before -- an item moved into a
group could not be moved back), copy it out to General, and copy a vault item
INTO the group. Without the membership the group tier resolves to no mounts,
so the first two would 404 exactly as they did pre-fix.
P4.D112 (v4 d7263f39 + f6a10055) adds the EXPLICIT SOURCE container, the
components: move|copy|none mode, the title-carrying collision sentence, and
the post-write read-back verification. The fixture gains a four-item
composite family in the SOURCE character's vault (Coat + Cufflinks leaves,
Formal set nesting Cufflinks + the General archetype -- the shared-tier
piece that must NEVER travel -- and Sunday Best bundling Coat + Formal
set), plus a project-store item sharing Coat's id (the component-collision
refusal seed). Scenarios cover: explicit group source (no character
probing); move+components:move (ids kept, literal-compared -- the
UUID-normalizer-blindness rule); move/copy+components:copy (minted ids
remapped into componentItemIds); the copy+components:move refine refusal;
the destination component-collision refusal (nothing written); the
components-omitted guard whose UUID refs cannot resolve at the destination
-- the read-back pin (unresolvedComponentIds, literal both sides); and the
parse tri-states (source: null, components: null, neither-source + both
refines joined). The legacy collision scenario's sentence moves to v4's
title-carrying form. The oracle also emits a __destinations GET row (the
enumerate_destinations unchanged-check).
